name: metagpt-sop-pipeline
context: Multi-agent systems that mimic software team SOPs by assigning agents to sequential pipeline stages (e.g., requirements → architecture → coding → testing → review). Unlike role-play (autonomous dialogue) or supervisor-worker (dynamic delegation), SOP-pipeline agents execute fixed role-based stages in order. Each stage has a defined output artifact that feeds the next stage, providing structure, predictability, and auditability.
benefits: Structured pipeline provides predictable latency and cost
Each stage has clear input/output contracts
Role assignments are explicit and auditable
Failure isolation — one stage failure doesn't corrupt the whole pipeline
tradeoffs: Fixed pipeline cannot adapt to unexpected task structure
Requires careful SOP design for each task type
Not suitable for exploratory or open-ended tasks
use_cases: Automated code generation with code-review pipeline
Research report writing with structured authoring stages
Data analysis pipeline with ingest-transform-report stages
avoid_when: Tasks require dynamic branching or conditional execution
Exploratory tasks without a defined end state
anti_patterns: Relying on free-text stage outputs that downstream stages must parse
design_principles: Define minimal stages — only those necessary for the task type
Each stage output must have a machine-readable schema
Include a gate/validation step between every two stages
best_practices: Limit each stage to a single well-defined role
Validate stage outputs against a schema before passing to the next stage
Log each stage's input, output, and execution time for cost attribution
references: Hong et al., MetaGPT: Meta Programming for A Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework, 2023 — https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.00352
